title: Sparsity-paced session pricing notes
content:
Context / goal:
- Quick back-of-envelope for a session-focused pricing experiment that rewards sparse token usage and tolerates graceful degradation when cost spikes.
- Audience: PM + growth + solutions SEs who want a pay-as-you-go session product for chat UIs.
- Keep simple knobs: base-session credit, token burn rate, sparsity bonus, fallback surcharge.

Assumptions (rough, changeable):
- Spot GPU cost mapped to tokens: assume an amortized price of $0.22 / 1k tokens at current model (mid-sized open model quantized) for steady-state throughput. (This includes infra, memory, and amortized ops.)
- Peak penalty / burst: +40% cost when autoscale into burst capacity / higher tier GPUs.
- Typical session length: 6 exchanges, 750 tokens total (avg). Heavy session: 2k tokens. Micro session: 180 tokens.
- Desired gross margin target for hosted: 65% at scale (so price should be ~2.85x cost).

Design primitives:
1) Base session credit: every new conversation start uses 1 base-credit (covers routing, KV warm, chat context overhead). Price: $0.01 (initial anchor).
2) Token burn per session: charge X per 1k tokens; tiered bands with decreasing marginal price for higher volumes (to encourage retention).
3) Sparsity bonus: if the session has >40% system-side caching hits (prefix reuse / small delta tokens per turn) give a rebate of Y% of token charge.
4) Graceful-degradation subsidy: if system routes to fallback (cheaper but lower-quality model) during capacity constraints, offer a small credit to customer per affected request to keep UX intact.

Back-of-envelope scenarios:
- Price per 1k tokens (anchor): $0.75 / 1k (targeting 65% gross margin from $0.22 cost)
  - calculation: cost 0.22 => price = cost / (1 - margin) = 0.22 / (1 - 0.65) = 0.628 -> round up to $0.75 as pricing anchor and to give room for burst spikes
- Base-session credit: $0.01 applied on session start. For short sessions (180 tokens) total charges: base 0.01 + tokens (0.18*0.75) = 0.01 + 0.135 = $0.145 => effective markup on short sessions is higher but acceptable if used infrequently.

Examples:
A) Typical session (750 tokens)
- token charge: 0.75 * 0.75 = $0.5625
- base: $0.01
- subtotal: $0.5725
- if sparsity bonus applies (20% rebate): -$0.1125 => final $0.46
- implied gross margin: cost = 0.75 * 0.22 = $0.165 -> margin ~64%

B) Heavy session (2,000 tokens) with caching benefit 30%
- token charge: 2.0 * 0.75 = $1.50
- base: $0.01
- rebate (30%): -$0.45 -> final $1.06
- cost = 2.0 * 0.22 = $0.44 -> margin ~58% (still acceptable if most heavy sessions are cache-augmented)

C) Burst fallback event (10% of requests hit fallback cheaper model, charged same price but we apply small credit $0.02 per affected exchange):
- operational hit: assume fallback model cost half (0.11/1k) but extra ops/latency penalties + SLA credits => net extra cost to us: $0.03 per affected request. If we credit user $0.02, net retention win likely outweighs credit cost.

Sparsity detection heuristics (quick):
- Turn-level token delta < 30 tokens over 3+ consecutive turns = high reuse; mark as 'sparse'
- KV prefix match ratio > 0.6 => apply bonus
- Implement metric in console as "sparsity_ratio" and surface for customers to understand credits.

Pricing knobs and experiments (A/B ideas):
- A: Fixed price per 1k tokens ($0.75) + base session credit $0.01 + sparsity rebate 20% after threshold.
- B: Session-bundles: buy 10 session credits for $1.2 (approx 20% discount over on-demand) targeted at SMB chat apps.
- C: Surge-protection add-on: reserve a burst buffer for $50/month that limits fallback events; customers buying this get 50% smaller grace credits.

Open questions / risks:
- Is $0.75/1k too high vs market comparables? We should run a quick competitor parity check (OpenAI, Anthropic public pricing, other hosted providers) and see position.
- Complexity: sparsity bonus adds billing complexity and edge cases; need to ensure the console displays expected credits per session or customers will be confused.
- Cache fraud: customers could attempt to game cache hits; need heuristics that consider actual token reuse vs synthetic repetition.
- Accounting reconciliation: rebate mechanics must flow cleanly into invoicing and not cause negative line items.

To-do / next steps (quick):
- Spike: simulate 100k sessions using existing telemetry to estimate expected rebate burn given current caching stats. (Owner: Liam)
- Draft UI copy for credits and how sparsity bonus works (Owner: Sofia)
- Run competitor pricing scan and prepare a 2-slide summary (Owner: Aisha)
- Prototype metric (sparcity_ratio, fallback_count) in the console and expose to a small set of beta customers.

Notes to self (fragments):
- Could combine with session timeouts: long idle sessions cost base + keepalive-per-minute microcharge (tiny) to prevent stale long-chat abuse.
- Consider per-route override: some routes (support flows) should be billed differently because cost per resolution is higher.
- Revisit margin goal for Dedicated customers (lower per-token price negotiated in contracts).

References / links (internal):
- Confluence: /pricing/session-pricing-ideas (placeholder)
- Slack thread: #pricing-discuss (search: sparsity bonus)

Random quick math sanity checks (scratch):
- If average token per session drops from 750 -> 600 because sparsity caching improves, US savings = (150 tokens * $0.22/1k) = $0.033 per session cost reduction; multiply by 1M sessions ~= $33k cost savings.
- If rebate uptake is 10% of sessions at 20% rebate -> revenue reduction = 0.1 * 0.2 * revenue_from_tokens (approx small).

End of scratchpad.

-- Aisha
